summary: In a major commercial spaceflight milestone, SpaceX successfully captured a returning Starship spacecraft using launch pad tower arms for the first time during Flight 15, while company leadership outlined plans for a larger next-generation V4 model. In civil space news, NASA placed the Sentinel-6B satellite into Earth orbit, achieved its 16th consecutive clean financial audit, and noted that the interstellar probe Voyager 1 is nearing a distance milestone of one light-day from Earth. Planetary science operations advanced on Mars with NASA's Perseverance rover analyzing water-altered rock remnants and Curiosity logging 49 drill holes, while the fully online Simons Observatory and Euclid space telescope expanded astronomical observations. In military and defense developments, Senate appropriators unveiled a $1.1 trillion Pentagon spending bill as the Department of Defense failed its ninth consecutive audit, SpaceNukes opened a Los Alamos facility to build next-generation space reactors, and tracking firm LeoLabs acquired FishEye to strengthen missile defense capabilities. Concerns over U.S. military launch capacity also intensified following a recent Vulcan rocket failure, while the U.S. Air Force received its first permanent F-15EX at Kadena Air Base and outlined fleet connectivity upgrades. Internationally, King Charles III championed a new initiative focused on space sustainability. Looking ahead, skywatchers can watch for the peak of the annual Leonid meteor shower on Nov. 17–18.
